messages:
maya: Heads up — perf spike in prod since the 03/18 deploy. compile-queue length spiking and p99 token latency doubled for short-seq models.
jon: Where are you seeing the spike? Which metrics?
maya: Quick snapshot: compile_queue_len: 0.06 -> 4.8 over 20m; compiles/sec +9x; kv_cache_evictions up 3x. Seen on region-us-west.
sasha: Is this related to the autotune heuristic change from PR-4821? That changed kernel selection preferences right?
maya: Yes — autotune now biases toward the "throughput" kernel even for seq<=64 when warmup flags are off. Seems to pick a heavier kernel shape that triggers full JIT compiles repeatedly because cache keys don't match.
tasha: CI flagged a perf regression yesterday on runtime-integration perf-suite (job 703). That job failed with higher compile latency. We should bisect to the merge.
jon: Starting bisection now. First pass: master@abc123 -> PR-4821 merge. Repro on canary with the same config.
ci-bot: :warning: perf-alert: runtime/compile_queue > threshold (prod-us-west). Report: https://perf.redwood/internal/compare?run=703&alert=compile_queue
sasha: Paste log snippet from canary instance 34:
```
[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] compile-request trace=tr-9f3a kernel=throughput_v2 model=llama2-short seq_len=32 autotune=autopick
[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] kvcache: miss key=kv:llama2-short:throughput_v2:32
[2026-03-18T08:12:04Z] compile-start id=cmp-7a1d duration_est=1.2s
[2026-03-18T08:12:05Z] compile-finish id=cmp-7a1d size=18MB
```
Looks like the throughput kernel has a different KV key shape so existing prefix/KV entries don't match -> full compile.
maya: That explains the compile storm. Many short requests that used to hit the small-latency kernel now pick throughput -> cold compile repeatedly, queue backs up.
jon: Can we mitigate without full revert? Maybe force the heuristic to prefer latency kernel for seq<=64 via runtime flag, or increase compile backoff TTL so we don't recompile within X minutes.
tasha: Ops note: we have a rollout hold available. Recommend hold and fast revert if possible. I'll request hold on prod rollout 2026-03-18-47.
eng-sre-bot: Canary hold requested for rollout prod-2026-03-18-47 by tasha. Status: ON_HOLD. Notifying release leads.
maya: Short-term mitigation options:
- Revert PR-4821 (fastest)
- Toggle runtime flag KERNEL_AUTOPICK_STRICT=false -> forces legacy behavior
- Increase COMPILE_BACKOFF_TTL from 60s -> 600s
- Prewarm KV cache for the new kernel in canary
Which is fastest?
jon: Toggle flag is quickest if config rollout is supported in <10m. Revert requires PR + CI (~30-45m). Backoff TTL change is low-risk and quick but just masks root cause.
sasha: Also: KV cache churn shows kvcache_write_rate x3 and eviction_rate x3. Root cause likely cache-key normalization: throughput kernel adds batch-dim suffix to key. We'll open runtime issue for cache key normalization.
maya: I'll file the issue and attach flamegraph and CPU profiles. Profiling link: https://perf.redwood/internal/profiles/llama2-short/2026-03-18
sasha: Filed runtime#992: "kvcache key mismatch when kernel variant adds batch-dim suffix -> cache misses and repeated compiles". Assigning to sasha and jon.
tasha: I'll open revert PR and also prepare a runtime-flag rollout as backup. Revert PR draft: https://git.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/549
jon: I can push the flag to canary now: set KERNEL_AUTOPICK_LEGACY=true for canary pool only. If canary stabilizes, we can roll to prod.
eng-sre-bot: Canary config update applied to pool=canary-34. Monitoring for 15m.
maya: After toggling flag, compile_queue dropped from 4.8 -> 0.2 in canary within 6m, p99 token latency back to baseline. Good sign.
tasha: Revert PR merged to staging, scheduling prod revert if canary remains green for 30m. If not, we'll escalate and revert immediately.
jon: Follow-up TODOs:
- sasha: root-cause patch for cache key normalization
- maya: add unit test for KV key shapes across kernel variants
- ops: add a canary runbook step to prewarm KV cache when adding new kernel variants
- eng-sre: add alert that pairs compile_queue spikes with kvcache_evictions
sasha: I'll start the patch. Also adding a compatibility layer to compute canonical keys.
maya: Thanks all. tagging @oncall for FYI: @jon @tasha
jon: I'll watch the canary for the next hour. If green, proceed with staged rollout of flag revert.
tasha: Revert deployed to prod at 2026-03-18T09:03Z. Monitoring.
maya: :thumbsup: will post a summary to #eng-runtime postmortem thread after we confirm stability.
